summary: Round-6 verify. Everything below MEASURED on the staged tree: each mutant applied to the worktree, run with `./gradlew :sequencer:test --tests 'binjava.sequencer.FaultInjectingStore*' --rerun-tasks` after deleting sequencer/build/test-results/test, every run bracketed by a sha256 of the three staged files so a concurrent edit could not fake a result, and every mutation reverted with `git checkout --`. Unmutated tree = 15 tests / 0 failures; staged diff still hashes 43185b5d8a07. CLOSED: W1 -- all three mutations it named now die (deleting putIfMatch's discarded unreachable draw and its discarded duplicate draw each fail everyClassDrawsOnEVERYFaultingCall...; moving putIfAbsent's duplicate draw below the throws fails aFIRINGClassDoesNotSHIFT... at seed 0). CLOSED: the parallel test review's wiring finding -- aliasing duplicateDraws onto stream 1 and ambiguousDraws onto stream 3 both fail eachClassIsWIREDToItsOWNStream..., and three distinct Randoms all on stream 1 fails it too; one SHARED Random object for all three fields also dies, but by the drawCounts test, not by the wiring test written for it (countDraw labels by object identity, so a shared object collapses three names into one) -- worth knowing because it means that kill would evaporate if countDraw ever took its name from the call site. CLOSED: W3 -- blanking the recorded key on putIfAbsent's unreachable arm, on putIfAbsent's ambiguous arm and on putIfMatch's ambiguous arm each fail EVERYClassRecordsWHICHKeyItFaultedOnTheWritePathToo. STILL OPEN as minors, unfixed and permitted to land under rule 11: W2 (firesAt still models the draw), W4 ('LANDS, THEN REPORTS FAILURE' still unconditional), W5 (both halves of the prose finding are still in the staged rows -- filed again below because the rows are in this diff). NEW: one major, on the row's test count, plus measured gaps in the two new tests. On drawCounts() as a fixture accessor: defensible. The decorator IS the unit under test here, and 'each class advances its own stream exactly once per conditional write' is part of its contract rather than an incidental implementation detail -- criterion 1's per-class attribution rests on it and nothing else can observe it, since a uniformly deleted draw shifts both arms of a toggle comparison alike. The problem is not the accessor, it is that the assertion built on it is weaker than its name (Y2). On the split into two classes: the seam is real and neither file is missing a fixture -- each has its own private body(), which is duplication of four trivial lines and the right call over a shared base class -- but the split left three javadoc blocks stranded on the wrong methods (Y4) and an unused import (Y5), and dropped the @Timeout the other eleven sequencer test classes carry (Y6). COST: no object-store request-rate finding. The decorator is test-only; the one request it adds is the deliberate second conditional PUT of the duplicatePut class, which scales with injected faults on segment writes, not with records, shards, partitions or indices, and the read verbs add none. ADR-0029: the M4.16 row's claim is accurate -- decisions/ holds exactly 0001-0028 and nothing in the tree references an ADR-0029 other than that line.

findings.line: 265 (the M4.12 row, 'the decorator and TWELVE unit tests of it')
findings.finding: THE COUNT IS WRONG AGAIN, and this is the third time the same sentence has been false. The staged tree has FIFTEEN @Test methods, not twelve: `git show :sequencer/.../FaultInjectingStoreTest.java | grep -c '^    @Test'` = 10 and the same on FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest = 5. The row also names no second file, so it describes a one-file commit that is not the one staged -- while its own next clause says 'an earlier draft of this row described a commit other than itself' and the clause after that says 'A COUNT IN PROSE GOES STALE EVERY TIME A REVIEW ROUND ADDS A TEST'. Round 5 closed this finding by verifying twelve against twelve; the W1 fix then added three tests and a file, and the row was not touched. The fix is to DELETE the number and name both classes, not to write 'fifteen' -- the row itself makes that argument, and a fourth count is a fourth thing to invalidate.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.15 is the milestone review, and milestone-review reads backlog.md, which AGENTS.md calls authoritative. A reviewer at M4's completion condition reads 'the decorator and TWELVE unit tests of it', greps one file, finds ten, and cannot tell whether five tests were added without a row update or three were deleted to make a gate pass -- the second being a non-negotiable-2 breach. The row exists precisely to let that check be made from the text, so a false count converts a two-second verification into re-deriving the commit from the log.

findings.finding: THE COUNTING TEST RUNS WITH `Faults.none()`, so it cannot see draw-vs-BRANCH order, and its name claims otherwise -- 'on EVERY FAULTING call' is asserted by a fixture in which no call ever faults. Two mutations MEASURED surviving all 15 tests. (a) Move putIfMatch's two result-discarding draws from above the `if (ambiguous)` block to below it -- i.e. the putIfMatch twin of exactly the lazy-draw defect W1 named on putIfAbsent, which the file's own comment calls the third-time-shipped property: counts stay 4/4/4 because with none() the throw is never taken, aFIRINGClassDoesNotSHIFT... drives putIfAbsent only, and the wiring test drives putIfAbsent only. (b) Swap the ambiguousPut/duplicatePut labels inside countDraw -- the only assertion has all three counts EQUAL, so any permutation of the labels passes, which means the accessor's per-class attribution, the whole point of it, is unpinned. (Also unpinned, same test: `return Map.copyOf(drawCounts)` -> `return drawCounts` survives, while the sibling injected() snapshot IS pinned by theInjectedRecordIsASNAPSHOT.) One assertion kills all three: drive an ASYMMETRIC mix with a fault ENABLED -- e.g. ambiguousPut = 1.0, two putIfAbsent (one throwing) plus one putIfMatch (throwing) plus one stat -- and assert unequal expected counts per class. Unequal counts pin the labels, the enabled fault pins the order against the throw, and including a read verb pins Y7 at the same time.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 adds delayed writes and reordered completions to putIfMatch and gives the lease CAS a clean-failure fault, which means editing that method's branch structure. Hoisting the ambiguous branch to the top -- the natural shape once there are four arms -- makes the lease-CAS path draw lazily again, so every putIfMatch that faults shifts the unreachable and duplicatePut streams behind it. The sweep then reports 'toggling duplicatePut changed seed N's outcome' when what changed was where ambiguousPut fired, and criterion 1's per-class attribution is fabricated with all 15 tests green -- the same defect this file has now shipped and fixed three times, arriving through the one verb the counting test cannot constrain.

findings.finding: THE WIRING IS PINNED ON THE WRITE PATH ONLY. MEASURED: re-pointing all three read verbs from `unreachableDraws` to `ambiguousDraws` -- `if (fires(ambiguousDraws, faults.unreachable()))` in stat, get and list, three lines -- survives all 15 tests. The new wiring test drives putIfAbsent exclusively, and theREADSideFaultsTooAndEVERYClassRecordsWHICHKeyItHit runs at p = 1.0 where every stream fires on every draw, so which stream the read verbs consume is unconstrained by anything. The test's name and its 'THROUGH THE STORE, one class enabled at a time' comment are scoped to neither verb, so the claim reads wider than what it checks -- and the M4.12 row lists 'the read-side verbs' among what this commit covers.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 owns giving getRange and the remaining verbs faults. A copy-paste of the existing `if (fires(unreachableDraws, ...))` block that lands on the wrong field -- one identifier, no compiler complaint, no test failure -- correlates read-path unreachability with write-path ambiguity. `recover`'s chain walk is all reads, so the sweep that exists to fault RECOVERY would fail its GETs exactly when ambiguousPut fires on its PUTs, and every seed that violates an invariant would be attributed to the wrong fault class while the harness reports per-class independence.

findings.finding: THE SPLIT LEFT THREE JAVADOC BLOCKS STRANDED, each now attached to a test it does not describe. 'Whether stream {@code stream} for {@code seed} fires on its {@code draw}-th draw.' now documents aProbabilityOUTSIDEZeroToOneIsREFUSED...; 'Drives a fixed call sequence and records which call index EACH class fired on' -- with a nine-line note about attribution by injected() growth -- now documents theREADSideFaultsTooAndEVERYClassRecordsWHICHKeyItHit; 'The call indexes at which {@code kind} fired... p = 0.9 rather than 0.05... which is what makes {@code isNotEqualTo} a real discriminator' now documents EVERYClassRecordsWHICHKeyItFaultedOnTheWritePathToo, a test containing no isNotEqualTo and no probability below 1.0. The methods they described (firesAt, firedIndexesWith, callsWhereOnly) went to FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest; their doc comments did not.
findings.failure_scenario: Javadoc and every IDE bind a doc comment to the declaration that follows it, so a reader (or an agent doing next-task) asking why the write-path key test uses p = 0.9 reads an explanation of a discriminator that is not in that test, and a reader of the probability-guard test is told it measures a stream. This is the same failure the M4.3 rounds recorded as a class javadoc still carrying a defence a later round had refuted: prose that argues about code that is no longer beneath it, in the file that is supposed to make the fixture believable.

findings.finding: `import java.util.ArrayList;` is unused -- the only ArrayList uses went to FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest with the helpers. No gate covers it (there is no Checkstyle/ErrorProne unused-import rule wired), so it will sit there.
findings.failure_scenario: Trivial on its own; it matters as the marker of an incomplete split alongside Y4 -- the next reader who greps this file for what it still needs is told it builds lists, and the leftover is evidence that nothing checked the file after the move.

findings.finding: THE SPLIT DROPPED THE TIMEOUT. FaultInjectingStoreTest keeps `@Timeout(value = 60, threadMode = SEPARATE_THREAD)` (line 30), and so do all ten other test classes in sequencer/src/test; the new file is the only one without it, and it is the one holding every unbounded-ish loop -- 20,000 seeds x 3 pairs x 4 draws in theTHREEFaultStreamsAreINDEPENDENTCoins, 25 x 120 store calls in aFIRINGClassDoesNotSHIFT. It runs in 0.146s today, so this is about the failure mode, not the budget.
findings.failure_scenario: build.md asks for a timeout so a hung test releases its memory, and M4.3c's round-1 review already paid for this lesson here: after bounding its waits, 'the putIfAbsent -> put mutation now names a failing test in 12s instead of hanging out the 10-minute Gradle task timeout'. Raise `seeds` while chasing a phase-lock, or let a future fault class loop on a retry, and this file hangs the whole :sequencer:test task for ten minutes and reports a task failure with no test name, instead of failing one test in sixty seconds.

findings.finding: W5 IS NOT FIXED -- both halves are still in the staged prose. (a) The M4.20 row still splices the deliverable onto a defect note: 'Also `withZone` returns `this`, violating the `Clock` contract -- many logical pods, one seed, through the `Sequencer` seam, with failover both ways (a polite release and a TTL lapse) and fenced leaders that do not know it yet.' The clause after the dash is what the driver must DO; it now reads as a consequence of the withZone bug. (b) The M4.16 row still says '⚠️ PINNED, not skipped: M4.13's sweep asserts exactly the known-failing seeds and no others, so the defect cannot silently grow while it waits' in the present tense about a row whose own status is todo -- there is no sweep, so nothing pins the defect.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Whoever picks up M4.20 reads the row for its acceptance criteria and finds them grammatically subordinate to a Clock-contract nit, so 'failover both ways' can be read as describing SimulatedClock rather than the driver, and the criterion that the driver must exercise a polite release AND a TTL lapse is the one most likely to be dropped. (b) A reader of M4.16 concludes the I2 violation is currently pinned by an asserting sweep and defers it with confidence; in fact the violation can widen -- more seeds, new mechanisms -- with the whole suite green until M4.13 is written.

findings.finding: THE TWO NEW ROWS ASSERT PRESENT-TENSE FACTS ABOUT FILES THE TREE DOES NOT CONTAIN. After this commit, `git ls-files sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer` holds no Invariants.java, no InvariantsTest.java, no CommitProtocolSimulation.java and no SimulatedClock.java -- they are untracked in this working copy only. Yet M4.19 says 'The remaining work is FIXTURES', that four named predicates 'each survive deletion with the whole suite green', that 'crossEpochOffsetsChecked() is a hard-coded true with an assertion around it' and that 'two fixtures build a LeaseManager on Clock.systemUTC()'; M4.20 says 'withZone returns this' and that 'the harness's own comment cites 6 commits and 3 takeovers'. This is the shape the M4.16 row itself now warns about after the ADR-0029 finding: 'nothing in the tree may rest on a draft the tree cannot see'.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone who clones the repo at this commit and runs next-task on M4.19 reads 'the remaining work is FIXTURES', plans a test-only commit, and then discovers the production class does not exist -- the row understates the deliverable by the entire checker. If the follow-up commits never land (a lost session, a discarded branch), both rows describe measurements of code no one can find, and the mutation counts they cite as their argument are unverifiable from the tree.
